summary: Smith Peak in Boundary County had a 1925 survey camp and a 1928 Fickes L-2 cab, staffed in the 1930s, and was in ruins by the 1950s.

facts.design: Fickes L-2 Special cab, a half-price version of the D-6 cupola (1928)
facts.status_note: In ruins by the 1950s; Idaho Fire Lookouts lists the site as hike-in ruins.

visit.trail_note: Idaho Fire Lookouts lists the site as hike-in ruins.

events.note: A camp with an alidade was developed at the site; Idaho Fire Lookouts names Clarence Kauffman as staffing it.
A Clyde Fickes L-2 Special cab was built.
Bill Edwards is tied to a 1933 Bonners Ferry Herald item.
Jonas Parshall is listed for 1934; Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 1934-1935.
In ruins by the 1950s; the exact year is not given.

evidence.supports: About 18 miles northwest of Bonners Ferry
Camp and alidade developed at the site in 1925
evidence.quote: A camp and alidade were developed here in 1925.

corrections.why: Both sources describe ruins by the 1950s rather than a full removal, and Idaho Fire Lookouts still lists Hike-In Ruins.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FireLookout.com lists Jonas Parshall for 1934 only; Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 1934-1935 and also names Bill Edwards for 1933. The story lists both.
The builder's name is spelled Fickes on FireLookout.com and Flickes on Idaho Fire Lookouts. The record uses Fickes, the spelling on FireLookout.com.

notes_for_editor: Kaniksu National Forest appears on all three pages; Boundary County appears on FireLookout.com and Rex's page. The Smith Peak in Plumas County, California is a different lookout and was excluded. A search result gave a 1929 L-2 design date from a blog; it was not used because it is unverified. The 1925 Kauffman staffing comes from a Fire Lookout Museum credit cited on Idaho Fire Lookouts. The 'Hike-In Ruins' tag is not treated as a current access statement, so no visit facts are recorded.
